prompt:
A single mobile web page screen, portrait, 1024x1536, rendered edge to edge as the page itself (no phone frame, no browser chrome). "Oozedle": a daily game for the college ultimate team Ooze; it hides one player's stat line from one tournament; six guesses; each guess shows only an up arrow (hidden player had more), down arrow (fewer) or equals sign per stat. A working game screen of standard web controls.

Regions, top to bottom:
1. Slim top bar: wordmark "OOZEDLE" left; links "Players", "Tournaments" right; a small tag at far right edge below it "#214 · Tue Oct 21".
2. The focal moment: the hidden stat line posted like the empty final slot at the top of a tournament bracket. A heavy-ruled box labelled above in the condensed face "PDQ 2026 — WHO HAD THIS LINE?"; inside, five large square cells in a row, each with a small label beneath ("PP", "A", "G", "B", "T") and a huge "?" in the heavy condensed face; cells already solved by an equals guess show the confirmed sign as a solid ink block (T, A, G and B solved: show their "=" blocks filled; PP still "?").
3. Below it, bracket lines feed up into that slot: three played guesses as ruled bracket rows, each a struck-through name with five small arrow/equals marks aligned under the five slot cells:
   Rowan: PP up, A down, G up, B down, T equals
   Farmer: PP down, A equals, G up, B down, T up
   Colin: PP up, A down, G equals, B equals, T down
   Then "3 guesses left" in small text with three short empty bracket stubs.
4. Guess control low within thumb reach: input "Guess a player" and a marker-orange "Guess" button.

Visual world (fixed): the laminated schedule and bracket sheet zip-tied to the fence at a college ultimate tournament, translated into a clean, flat web screen. Ground is white board stock #f6f5f0; ink #141414; one marker-orange accent #ff5a1f used sparingly; thin rules #d9d7cf and heavy black bracket rules. One heavy condensed grotesk numeral/display face does every job from giant numbers to table heads; body text in a plain grotesk. Arrows are heavy black glyphs; equals cells are solid ink blocks with a white "="; wrong-guess names are struck through, never removed. No textures, no zip ties drawn, no shadows, no gradients, no photos, no mascots.
